**Published online:**
2026-08-26

**Geographic focus:**
North America, United States (Washington D.C. / Federal Reserve)

**Temporal focus:**
T1. Historical observation [YES] — Prior firing attempts, Cook case history, Powell tenure
T2. Forward-looking immediate [YES] — Cook dismissal deadline, Jefferson's 2026 decision, Atlanta Fed vacancy
T3. Long-term development [YES] — Board composition through 2028–2038, sustained Trump Fed influence strategy

**Synopsis:**
Trump's campaign to reshape Fed monetary policy through personnel control faces multiple fronts. The Cook firing case (pretext: mortgage document misstatement) returns to district court after SCOTUS ruling; outcome remains uncertain but Cook likely stays seated near-term. Powell remains on the board until early 2028. VP Jefferson's 2026 leadership term expiry is a key swing variable — his departure would open a seat; his stay would constrain Trump's vice chair options to Bowman or Waller. The Atlanta Fed presidency vacancy adds another lever. Warsh meanwhile has sidelined rate guidance entirely, resisting Trump's rate-cut pressure. The article paints a protracted, multi-year battle for Fed control with no near-term resolution.
